newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian president quits rally for security fears.
newsitem.headline: Albanian president quits rally for security fears.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha arrived in Tirana's main square to address an anti-violence rally on Tuesday but was rushed from the scene by bodyguards who were worried about his security, eyewitnesses said.

An ethusiatic but peaceful crowd of around 6,000 people surged forward when Berisha made his way on foot to the central Skanderbeg Square. It appeared the bodyguards were unable to prevent his supporters from approaching him.

Fearing the situation could get out of control, security guards rushed the president, who is a founder of the ruling right-wing Democratic Party, up the steps of the nearby Palace of Culture and inside the building.
He had been expected to address the crowd but waited inside the building surrounded by bodyguards for about 20 minutes before leaving by a back entrance.

"We want Berisha... We want Berisha," the crowd shouted. But the mayor of Tirana, Albert Brojka, later spoke to supporters telling them to disperse peacefully. Traffic was allowed back on roads around the square within minutes.
Three cordons of riot police stood in front of the opposition Socialist Party headquarters, sited across from the Palace of Culture, to prevent the crowd moving towards the rival party building.
